title: Django: project, apps, urls and views

videos.script: In lesson 1, Django answered one URL from a project you threw away. Today the real project starts, and it stays until the end of the course. {{project}} A Django project is two things. A settings file, which is ordinary Python. And manage.py, which runs commands against those settings. {{settings}} The code lives in apps. Each app is a folder with a job you can say in one sentence. Ours is called events. {{app}} Then the trip a request makes. The project's URL table hands everything under events to the app. The app's table picks a view. The view is a function, it gets the request, and it returns a response. {{urls}} Around that view sits a stack of middleware. Every request goes down through it, and every response comes back up. {{onion}} You write one layer yourself, a stopwatch. And you watch another layer refuse a POST before your view is even called. {{csrf}} Finally, the same view written as a class. It does the same work, with the HTTP methods handled for you. {{class}} By the end, agenda answers three URLs with JSON, and you can say which piece of Django handled each part of the answer.
